channel.title: Cloud Platform Brief
channel.description: Consequential developments for cloud and platform architects.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 7
item.description: Security and platform standardization dominate this week. GKE operators should urgently patch for compromised CA keys, and locked-down GitHub Actions environments must allow new blob endpoints. AWS launched managed ECS ingress and context-aware code vulnerability remediation; GitHub expanded enterprise GitHub App governance, OpenTofu shipped a security-fixing patch, and GCP added enforceable Model Armor baselines. Azure, upstream Kubernetes, Terraform, Pulumi, and Crossplane produced no additional release above the threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 6
item.description: This week brings two migration deadlines and several architectural shifts. Azure has retired GPv1 and legacy Blob accounts, while GitHub will remove three Copilot models on November 16; both require immediate inventory and owner assignment. AWS introduces HTTP-native Lambda Web Functions and richer log routing, GCP makes service perimeters hierarchy-aware, and GitHub operationalizes agentic code-scanning fixes. Kubernetes and the main IaC projects produced no release that cleared the threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 5
item.description: This week shifts from broad feature launches to governance and controlled change. Pulumi’s GCP provider 10.0 introduces replacements and removals that demand stack-by-stack testing, while GitHub makes local agent sandboxing enforceable and previews credit-backed AI secret checks. Azure changes Kubernetes posture findings at controller scope; AWS adds sovereignty guidance and useful multicloud and DevOps-agent patterns. No upstream Kubernetes or Terraform/OpenTofu release cleared the threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 4
item.description: This week is led by lifecycle and upgrade pressure: AWS announced multiple service sunsets, GitHub began enforcing minimum self-hosted runner versions, and GitHub data-residency clients face an October 7 TLS deadline. OpenTofu 1.13 and EKS 1.37 both require deliberate compatibility testing, while GKE previews coordinated HPA/VPA rightsizing. AWS also previewed architecture remediation with AI; Azure produced no release that cleared the editorial threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 3
item.description: Architecture teams have an unusually dense week: AWS reshaped event-driven integration, added multi-cloud AI inventory, and introduced GPU-aware inference routing, while GKE advanced both node density and sidecarless service networking. Immediate attention belongs on GitHub Actions’ completed Node 20 retirement and Crossplane 2.4.2’s ownership and security fixes. Azure and the main Terraform/OpenTofu tracks produced no additional release that cleared the editorial threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 2
item.description: This week is dominated by control-plane hardening and migration work: GCP made SPIFFE-based backend mTLS generally available, changed Model Armor defaults with a December retirement deadline, and introduced a breaking Agent Platform SDK boundary. Crossplane operators should patch, while Kubernetes teams should benchmark the new resource-management behavior before enabling it. No AWS or Azure release cleared the editorial threshold.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Launch preview
item.description: The dashboard is ready. Automated weekly editions begin after repository setup.

item.title: Cloud Platform Brief — Issue 1
item.description: Kubernetes 1.37 introduces alpha controls for hardening writable volumes. GitHub expands enterprise security enforcement, AI-development governance and automated coverage policies, while GCP changes the default representation for MongoDB-to-BigQuery streams. Architecture teams should review Kubernetes feature-gate pilots and validate downstream schemas before creating new Datastream pipelines. No AWS or Azure changes met the editorial threshold this week.
